timed_text.text: Day 15. Your focus anchor — the word your mind returns to when it drifts.
The most powerful anchor isn't just a word in your head — it's physical.
Elite athletes do this instinctively. They're trained focus triggers.
The key is consistency — the same thing, the same way, every single time.
Do it enough times in a focused state and it begins to trigger the state.
Think about the physical environment where you compete.
What is something you can see, touch, feel or do?
Something always available in that space — that's your competition anchor.
On your screen, you're going to identify it and lock it in.

cards.prompt: Think about the physical space where you compete. What do you see, hear, or feel in that environment that is always there — every competition, every time?

Identify your physical anchor — something in that space, or something you wear or carry, that you can use as a consistent focus trigger. Something you can touch, see, or do deliberately before or during competition.
Design the moment — exactly when in competition will you use this anchor? Between plays? Before the starting signal? After a mistake? Write the specific moment and the exact action.
Say your focus word once. Feel your attention settle. That word plus that physical anchor — those two together are your return to center.

timed_text.text: Every rep with that anchor strengthens the link to your focused state.
Do it in practice, do it in warmups, do it in competition.
The more consistent you are, the faster it works when the pressure is real.
Check out the journal and have to finish.

blocks.prompt: What physical anchor did you choose — and why does that specific thing feel right for your competition environment?
